lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p16 - Listen and draw.

details: Listen and draw reviews the target language and key structure from the unit and helps students practise listening for detail.
Look for careful listening, correct identification of which item of furniture to draw and which room to draw it in.

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p16 - 2 & 3. Draw your house. Compare with a friend. Ask and answer Where is … ?

details: Draw your house gives students freer practice of the target language and key structure in a more personalised and engaging way. It allows students to strengthen oral fluency and apply the target language in a way that is relevant in a real-world context.

Look for recognisable items of furniture drawn in appropriate rooms, clear pronunciation, stress and intonation when asking and answering questions, accurate use of the target language and key structure, and natural turn-taking with classmates.

Heads Up:
